title: A Son in His Own Likeness

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Adam had lived 130 years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image; and he named him Seth. After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters. Altogether, Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died. - Gen 5:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a quiet shift in wording here. God made Adam "in the likeness of God" (v.1), but Adam had a son "in his own likeness, in his own image." Seth bore not only the image of God but also the fallen image of his father - including sin and mortality. The likeness of God remained, but now it passed down cracked and broken.

And then come three sombre words that will echo through the whole chapter: "and then he died." Adam lived 930 remarkable years, yet the sentence God warned of came true. Death had entered the world, just as He said (Gen 2:17). No length of life could outrun it.

This is honest, sobering truth. We inherit both the dignity of God's image and the brokenness of Adam's fall. We are glorious and mortal all at once.

But the story does not end at the grave. Where Adam brought death to all, Christ - the second Adam - brings life to all who trust Him (1 Cor 15:22). One day, believers will bear the image of the risen Christ fully (1 Cor 15:49). The likeness Adam passed on ends in death; the likeness Christ gives ends in resurrection.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you living with the reality that your days here will end?
- Have you found your hope in Christ, the second Adam?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am mortal, made from dust, yet made in Your image. Thank You that in Christ my death is not the end but the doorway to life.
